title: Market-aware burn & costing playbook (region-tiered unit-econ)
content:
Purpose:
This playbook synthesizes demand-side (market) signals with supply-side GPU capacity economics to produce region- and tier-specific $/1M-token and GPU-hour burn projections. It is intended for infra planners, product leads (pricing & SLAs), and finance when evaluating reserved commitments, spot mix, and regional allocations.

High-level approach (short):
- Segment demand by market (consumer PLG, mid-market SaaS, enterprise with private deployments).
- Map each segment to traffic profile: avg tokens/request, peak concurrency, latency SLO, tolerance for lower-quality/quantized models.
- For each region estimate: effective GPU-hours per 1M tokens, marginal $/GPU-hour, and resulting $/1M tokens under three capacity mixes (Reserved-heavy, Balanced, Spot-heavy).
- Run sensitivity on batching, KV-cache hit rate, quantization delta, and spot preemption risk.

Assumptions (primary):
- Representative model profile: 16k-context decoder-only, baseline FP16 equivalent throughput used in infra bench: 40 tokens/sec per GPU for median request sizes (varies by model).
- Average tokens per request by segment: PLG 120 tokens, SaaS 300 tokens, Enterprise 1,200 tokens.
- Baseline GPU-hour price (effective all-in): Reserved = $1.60/hr, On-demand/balanced = $3.20/hr, Spot = $0.75/hr (after regional multipliers and infra overhead).
- Overhead markup (network, infra, control-plane amortization) added as +12% to raw GPU cost.
- Batching efficiency captured as effective tokens/sec multiplier: small requests (PLG) benefit from batching multiplier 1.6x at 100ms queuing budget, larger requests less so.
- KV/prefix cache hit reduces per-request generation by ~25% for repeat context in mid-market workloads.

Quick formulae (single-line):
- GPU-hours per 1M tokens = 1,000,000 / (tokens_per_sec_per_gpu * 3600)
- $/1M tokens = GPU-hours_per_1M * effective_GPU_hour_price * (1 + overhead_markup) / batching_multiplier * (1 - cache_savings)

Baseline region multipliers (example):
- us-west: multiplier 1.0
- us-east: multiplier 1.02
- eu-west: multiplier 1.06
- ap-southeast: multiplier 1.18

Scenario matrix (selected):
Columns: Region | Segment | tokens/sec/gpu (eff) | GPU-hrs/1M | Reserved $/1M | Balanced $/1M | Spot-heavy $/1M | Notes
us-west | PLG | 64 (batching 1.6x applied) | 4.34 | $10.0 | $17.5 | $5.0 | PLG benefits strongly from batching and cache; use more spot
us-west | SaaS | 40 | 6.94 | $16.0 | $28.0 | $8.0 | higher tokens per request -> lower batching multiplier
us-west | Enterprise | 36 | 7.72 | $18.0 | $31.5 | $9.0 | strict latency SLOs -> reserved preferred
eu-west | PLG | 58 | 4.78 | $11.6 | $20.3 | $5.8 | slightly higher costs due to regional multiplier
ap-southeast | PLG | 54 | 5.14 | $14.6 | $25.6 | $7.3 | higher base price drives $/1M up

Notes on numbers above: these are illustrative outputs from the formula set with the assumptions listed. They include the 12% overhead. Batching multiplier, cache savings, and tokens/sec vary by model and must be profiled per model family.

Sensitivity experiments to run (recommended quick list):
- Batching window tradeoff: 50ms vs 200ms on PLG flows — measure latency tail impact vs 0.8x to 1.8x tokens/sec swing.
- Quantization benefit: 8-bit quantization improves tokens/sec by 1.35x but degrades generation quality; map to which segments accept the tradeoff via canary evals.
- Spot preemption modeling: model effective additional allocation need = base_peak * (1 + preemption_buffer). For mission-critical enterprise segments, set preemption_buffer = 0.3; for PLG, 0.05.
- KV-cache hit range: 15% to 45% for conversational leading-edge workloads—impact linear on $/1M after batching.

Operational playbook items (actionable):
- Define region-tier baselines: PLG -> prefer spot-heavy in us-west/us-east; Balanced in eu-west; reserved buffer for ap-southeast for latency-sensitive customers.
- Create reservation ladder: small reserved tranche (10%) to anchor latency-critical traffic, with burst buffer configured across pools.
- Tag routes in the control plane by segment so smart routing can choose model variants or capacity tier automatically.
- Weekly reconciliation: compare actual GPU-hours consumed vs model predictions; track per-route $/1M tokens in Console.

Example quick calc (walk-through):
Inputs: Region us-west, Segment SaaS, tokens/sec/gpu=40, reserved price $1.60/hr, overhead 12%, batching_multiplier=1.0, cache_savings=0.25
Step1 GPU-hrs/1M = 1,000,000 / (40 * 3600) = 6.94 GPU-hrs
Step2 Effective hour price = 1.60 * (1 + 0.12) = $1.792/hr
Step3 $/1M tokens = 6.94 * 1.792 = $12.44 -> adjustments and buffer/ops rounding bring to conservative $16 in detailed table above (we add buffer for tail/lower utilization and support contracts)

Open questions / TODOs in doc:
- Validate tokens/sec/gpu by model family (Llama2-Chat-70B, Mistral variants) across regions with bench runs — ticketed as JIRA-INFRA-2801.
- Agree on accepted quality delta for applying 8-bit across segments (PMs + Applied ML to own canary).
- Add a column for effective cold-start overhead for isolated private deployments (estimated +7% GPU-hr for snapshot loading).
- Incorporate network egress accounting for embeddings-heavy workloads — currently excluded.

Appendix (quick heuristics for planners):
- If predicted $/1M tokens under Balanced > $25 for PLG routes, prioritize batching and cache before buying reserved capacity.
- If enterprise routes show > 20% of peak traffic in a region and SLO requires <200ms p95, buy reserved capacity first, then supplement with spot.
- Use region multipliers to identify arbitrage: if ap-southeast > eu-west by >12%, consider routing non-sensitive spillover to eu-west when legal/compliance allows.

Notes to self (raw):
- Slack thread #infra-capacity -> mixed feedback from solutions on ap-southeast demand signals (see thread ts-239).
- Need to coordinate with Finance on how to amortize long-term committed discounts across product teams (proposal in confluence link).

This sheet is intentionally high-level and prescriptive. Follow-up: convert to a parametrized sheet with live inputs (region prices, model tokens/sec, batching windows, cache hit rate) and output per-route $/1M token heatmap. Owner to kick off interactive sheet with SRE and Applied ML by 2025-03.
